summary: H. Munro Chadwick worked in linguistics, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Cambridge and Clare College, also studying under Wilhelm Streitberg. At Cambridge, he was Elrington and Bosworth Professor of Anglo-Saxon (1910–1941).
H. Schöhl specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Strasbourg, Munich, Göttingen, Freiburg, and Münster (PhD, by 1914), under teachers including Ernst Leumann and Richard Schmidt.
H. Sesha Aiyangar was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He held posts in the Kannaḍa and Canarese departments at the University of Madras, attested in 1938 and 1957.
H. V. Nagaraja Rao worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held positions at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore and as a professor at the University of Mysore (attested 2012).

Hae-ju Sunim is a Buddhist studies scholar. She served as a visiting lecturer at Harvard University (1996–1997) and as an associate professor of Buddhist studies at Dongguk University (attested 1999).

Haiyan Hu-von Hinüber works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. She earned an MA at Peking University by 1982 under Kemo Jin and also studied under Zhongxin Jiang. She was Director at the University of Freiburg in 2010.

Hajime Kitamura worked in linguistics and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tokan Tada. His posts included Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1964–1986), Reitaku University president (1986), and Toyo Bunko board chair (1990–2001).

Hajime Nakamura specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Hakuju Ui, later serving there as professor (1954–1973). He also founded and directed the Eastern Institute (Toho Gakuin) from around 1973 to 1999.

Hajime Okayama was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Tokyo, CASS, and Peking University under Xianlin Ji. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo from 1995 to 2012.

Hajime Sakurabe specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University under Issai Funahashi and Susumu Yamaguchi, later serving there as professor (1971–1986). He also taught at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1957–1959).

Philosopher Hajime Tanabe studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, and in Germany under Edmund Husserl, Heinrich Rickert, and Martin Heidegger. A disciple of Kitaro Nishida, he taught at Tohoku University and Kyoto University (1919–1945).
Hakuin Ekaku was an active figure in Buddhist studies who studied under Dōkyō Etan around 1708 and under Hakuyūshi around 1710–1711.

Hakuju Ui worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu, and abroad at Tübingen, Oxford, and Cambridge. He held teaching posts at Tokyo, Tohoku, and served as Komazawa University president (1941).

Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under teachers including Bokusan Nishiari, Kodo Akino, Ian Kishizawa, Tatsumoto Nozawa, and Sogaku Harada (1925–1943), and founded Sanbo Zen in 1954.
Hakuyu Hadano was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held posts at Tohoku University, including assistant professor (attested 1953–1959) and later professor emeritus.
Halina Marlewicz specializes in Indology and philosophy. She studied under Tadeusz Pobożniak and held a post as professor at Jagiellonian University.
Linguist Halina Safarewiczowa studied at Vilnius University (~1924–1928) and held a post at Jagiellonian University from approximately 1946 to 1974.

Halle O'Neal works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Kansas under Sherry Fowler (attested 2011) and holds a co-director post at the University of Edinburgh.

Hallvard Kåre Kuløy specialized in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He served as an officer at UNICEF (1972–1978, 1980–1984), edited Kailash (~1973), and founded Orchid Press and Bibliotheca Himalayica in 1982.

Hammalawa Saddhatissa specialized in Buddhist studies, earning degrees from Banaras Hindu University and the University of Edinburgh (PhD 1963). He headed the London Buddhist Vihara (~1957–1990) and taught at Banaras Hindu University, SOAS, and the University of Toronto (~1966–1969).
